body:
I did a cursory review, because I'm not really keen on this solution as is. I agree to introduce async sockets where the OS notifies Godot of changes, instead of Godot actively polling the OS for data. But this PR introduces a very specific async socket implementation only for Apple inside of DAP/LSP.

This is not a viable long-term solution; fixes like these should instead be done on the socket implementation code (now for Apple, but likely for other OSes in the future as well). DAP/LSP only consume the networking API, and should not care for those implementation details.

---
I also thought of something else that might mitigate this problem, specifically for Xogot. I'm not familiar with it, but I assume it's an iOS app with a completely integrated development environment, requiring no external tools for code editing & debugging. If that is correct, then you should not need LSP/DAP to begin with, so it would be good if you could disable these if indeed they are not useful.

LSP already has an `GDSCRIPT_NO_LSP` define that, if set, does not load the LSP module. I was under the impression DAP could also be easily disabled, but apparently that's not the case. As I assume you're building a custom version of Godot for Xogot, an idea would be to expose this to the build system, to allow anyone to disable them.

I am using LSP :-)

Anyways, I already have these fixes on my tree.  I am sharing these so the community can use them if they see fit.

currently Godot is just burning cpu non-stop for no good reason and burning battery time.

I went down this path because my own profiling was being dominated by this noise, and then noticed Godot was skipping an entire rendering frame due to dozens of things like this.  So I fixed them.

and then someone on rocket chat shared that leaving their laptop unplugged while doing dinner killed their battery and now it doesn’t.

see link for details
